book.title: Frankenstein · Chapter 1 — A Gift Called Elizabeth
book.author: Mary Shelley, Frankenstein (1818), Chapter 1

cast.name: Alphonse

cast.anchor: a short dark beard and a dignified long coat

cast.name: Beaufort
cast.canonical: a gaunt sunken balding grey man, clean-shaven, in a threadbare but once-fine coat, a proud broken bearing
cast.anchor: gaunt balding grey, clean-shaven, in a threadbare fine coat

cast.name: Caroline

cast.anchor: dark hair in a centre-parted bun, a cross necklace and a high-collar dark dress

cast.name: Victor
cast.canonical: a small young boy with tidy dark hair and tiny round glasses
cast.anchor: a small boy with tiny round glasses

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.canonical: a radiant little girl with bright flowing golden hair, angelic face
cast.anchor: a little girl with bright flowing golden hair

panels.scene: an elegant old Geneva townhouse, a dignified bearded man in a long coat standing proudly before it

teen.narration: OUR STORY BEGINS NOT WITH A MONSTER, BUT WITH A FAMILY. VICTOR’S FATHER, ALPHONSE, IS A RESPECTED MAN OF GENEVA.

bubbles.text: I am by birth a Genevese, and my family is one of the most distinguished of that republic. My ancestors had been for many years counsellors and syndics

panels.scene: a proud gaunt merchant in a threadbare fine coat turning his face away in shame, an empty grand room behind him

teen.narration: ALPHONSE’S DEAREST FRIEND, THE MERCHANT BEAUFORT, LOSES HIS FORTUNE — AND HIS PRIDE WON’T LET HIM BE PITIED.

bubbles.text: was of a proud and unbending disposition and could not bear to live in poverty and oblivion

panels.scene: a poor bare room; a young woman with a bun tends a thin sick old man on a bed

teen.narration: HE HIDES IN A MEAN LITTLE TOWN WITH HIS DAUGHTER, CAROLINE. IT TAKES ALPHONSE TEN MONTHS TO FIND THEM.

bubbles.text: it was ten months before my father discovered his abode

panels.scene: the young woman with a bun plaiting straw by candlelight, exhausted but resolute

teen.narration: CAROLINE IS EXTRAORDINARY: SHE WORKS HERSELF RAGGED TO KEEP THEM ALIVE.

bubbles.text: her courage rose to support her in her adversity. She procured plain work; she plaited straw

panels.scene: the young woman weeping over a coffin in the bare room, utterly alone

bubbles.text: her father died in her arms, leaving her an orphan and a beggar.

panels.scene: the bearded man entering the room and gently reaching a hand to the kneeling weeping woman

teen.narration: THEN ALPHONSE ARRIVES — LIKE A RESCUE.

bubbles.text: He came like a protecting spirit to the poor girl, who committed herself to his care; and after the interment of his friend he conducted her to Geneva and placed her under the protection of a relation.

panels.scene: a small tender wedding of the bearded man and the young woman with a bun

teen.narration: HE CARES FOR HER, AND IN TIME LOVE GROWS.

bubbles.text: Two years after this event Caroline became his wife.

panels.scene: the couple travelling a sunny Italian landscape, he shielding her gently under a parasol

teen.narration: HE CHERISHES HER LIKE SOMETHING RARE AND FRAGILE, TAKING HER TO ITALY TO HEAL.

bubbles.text: He strove to shelter her, as a fair exotic is sheltered by the gardener, from every rougher wind

panels.scene: the couple doting on a small dark-haired baby boy in a sunny room

teen.narration: AND SO VICTOR IS BORN — ADORED, THE CENTRE OF THEIR WORLD.

bubbles.text: I was their plaything and their idol, and something better—their child, the innocent and helpless creature bestowed on them by Heaven

panels.scene: the woman with a bun and a small boy stepping into a poor peasant cottage of ragged children by a lake

teen.narration: BY LAKE COMO, KIND CAROLINE VISITS THE POOR — A GUARDIAN ANGEL TO THE SUFFERING.

panels.scene: among dark-haired ragged children, one radiant little girl with bright flowing golden hair stands out like a light
panels.composition: medium, one child glowing among others

teen.narration: AND AMONG THE RAGGED CHILDREN, ONE SHINES LIKE GOLD.

bubbles.text: Her hair was the brightest living gold, and despite the poverty of her clothing, seemed to set a crown of distinction on her head.

panels.scene: a close, tender portrait of the golden-haired little girl, luminous and angelic

teen.narration: SHE IS NO PEASANT CHILD — A NOBLEMAN’S ORPHANED DAUGHTER, LEFT WITH THIS POOR FAMILY.

bubbles.text: a being heaven-sent, and bearing a celestial stamp in all her features

panels.scene: the golden little girl playing in a grand villa hall, radiant against the dark panelling
panels.composition: medium, radiant child in a fine hall

teen.narration: THE FAMILY TAKES HER IN. SHE BLOOMS AMONG THEM.

bubbles.text: fairer than a garden rose among dark-leaved brambles

panels.scene: the golden-haired girl and the small bespectacled boy holding hands, becoming inseparable

teen.narration: SHE BECOMES VICTOR’S CONSTANT COMPANION — HIS MORE THAN SISTER.

bubbles.text: Elizabeth Lavenza became the inmate of my parents' house—my more than sister

panels.scene: the mother with a bun presenting the golden-haired girl to the small bespectacled boy as a gift, both children shy and delighted

teen.narration: HIS MOTHER OFFERS HER AS A GIFT — AND LITTLE VICTOR TAKES THE WORD TO HEART FOREVER.

bubbles.speaker: caroline
bubbles.text: I have a pretty present for my Victor—tomorrow he shall have it.

bubbles.speaker: victor
bubbles.text: my more than sister, since till death she was to be mine only.
